definitions.explanation: Describes eggs (or occasionally other foods) that have been boiled until the yolk and white are completely set and firm.

examples.japanese: {固|かた}ゆで⟦{卵|たまご}→卵：02222_tamago⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}った→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
{固|かた}ゆで⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{十二分|じゅうにふん}ほど⟦{茹|ゆ}でる→茹でる：02324_yuderu⟧。
examples.english: Boil for about twelve minutes to make them hard-boiled.

examples.japanese: ⟦サラダ→サラダ：01364_sarada⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{半熟|はんじゅく}→半熟：11935_hanjuku⟧⟦より→より：09476_yori⟧{固|かた}ゆで⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{方|ほう}→方：01139_hou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{崩|くず}れなくて→崩れる：04248_kuzureru⟧⟦{使|つか}いやすい→使いやすい：30380_tsukaiyasui⟧。
examples.english: Hard-boiled eggs are easier to use in salads than soft-boiled ones since they don't fall apart.

notes:
Also written as {固茹|かたゆ}で. A cooking term composed of {固|かた} (hard, firm) and ⟦{茹|ゆ}で→茹でる：02324_yuderu⟧ (boiling). Almost always used in reference to eggs. Can function as a noun ({固|かた}ゆで⟦{卵|たまご}→卵：02222_tamago⟧) or as a descriptive modifier ({固|かた}ゆで⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {固|かた}ゆで⟦{卵|たまご}→卵：02222_tamago⟧: hard-boiled egg
- {固|かた}ゆで⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to hard-boil
- {固|かた}ゆで⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{卵|たまご}→卵：02222_tamago⟧: hard-boiled egg

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{半熟|はんじゅく}→半熟：11935_hanjuku⟧: soft-boiled, half-cooked — the opposite, with a runny yolk
- ⟦{温泉卵|おんせんたまご}→温泉卵：27857_onsentamago⟧: hot spring egg — egg with set white and runny yolk
- {茹|ゆ}で{卵|たまご}: boiled egg — general term, regardless of doneness
